q: Consider: 1-The quota clause is textually a reservation provision. 2-The Court rejects treating it as a mere exception derogating from job equality. 3-It covers backward classes inadequately represented in services. 4-It creates a universal right to quota for every disadvantaged group. Correct set?
expl: Text, doctrine and class all bounded.
why: The clause is textually a reservation provision, but the Court reads it as a facet of real equality, not a derogation. Its class is bounded: backward and inadequately represented. No universal right to quota exists for every disadvantaged group.
trapnote: 'Exception' language and 'universal right' language both fail.

q: Which statement best reflects the 2024 interpretation of the resource-ownership directive?
options: All private property is community resource
Only some resources qualify; private ownership alone is insufficient
The shield now covers all welfare laws
expl: Narrow reading: ownership form is not the test.
why: The Court held that not every privately owned resource is a material resource of the community, and addressed the continued narrow scope of the shield. The chain runs: directive text, community-resource meaning, private-property question, shield consequence.
trapnote: 'Narrowed 39(b)' alone is too vague; test the private-property holding.

q: A State provides 62% total quota across backward classes with no EWS component and no extraordinary conditions. Outcome?
options: Fails: non-EWS quota above the ceiling without extraordinary justification
Valid: ceiling applies only to EWS
why: The ceiling principle governs the backward-class compartment; only extraordinary far-flung conditions excuse breach. EWS sits in a separate compartment, which is absent here, so no escape route exists.
trapnote: Test the principle and the compartment, never the bare number.

q: Evaluate: 1-Hotel denial routes to the access clause. 2-Well denial routes to the same clause unconditionally. 3-School admission denial routes to admission-equality. 4-Private-home bias routes to the access clause. Correct set?
expl: Well needs funding+public use; home is outside.
why: Hotels fall in the no-funding-needed access sub-clause; wells need State maintenance plus public dedication; admissions belong to admission-equality; purely private homes fall outside the access clause.
trapnote: Each access fact-pattern has its own sub-clause and conditions.

q: A High Court administrative order transfers a judge's staff adversely; a judicial order convicts allegedly unfairly. Challenge routes?
options: Administrative via writs, judicial via appeal/review
why: The judiciary counts as State in its administrative and rule-making capacity, so writs lie there. Judicial adjudication is corrected through appeal and review, not through writs alleging rights breach.
trapnote: 'Judiciary under Art 12' without capacity-split is a half-truth.

q: Match: A-arbitrariness-enemy, B-fair-procedure, C-quota-method, D-balance-of-rights-welfare with P-1974 officer case, Q-1978 passport case, R-1992 Mandal case, S-1980 shield case. Code?
why: Each doctrine is anchored to its year and facts: unexplained transfer, seized passport, Mandal quotas, wide-shield cut. Swapped options test whether pairs or years were memorised in isolation.
trapnote: Memorise doctrine+year+fact as one unit, never alone.

q: A citizen accepts a foreign honour styled as a knighthood; a non-citizen office-holder accepts one with clearance. Position pair?
options: Citizen barred, office-holder permitted with consent
expl: Citizen bar is absolute; consent route is for office-holders.
why: Citizens face an outright bar regardless of consent; the consent mechanism serves non-citizens holding office. Knighthood is a title, distinct from excellence awards which take no prefix.
trapnote: Consent never rescues a citizen; award-vs-title is a separate axis.

q: Which mechanism suspends the citizen's right to move courts for stated rights during Emergency, distinct from immunities, force-modifications and law-shields?
expl: Suspension of remedy differs from immunity, modification and shield.
why: One mechanism suspends enforcement remedies temporarily; immunity protects office-holders; force-modification adjusts application; the welfare shield protects laws. Lumping them as generic exceptions destroys the doctrinal map.
trapnote: Ask what each doctrine DOES, not what family it resembles.

q: Three claims: 1-Awards and titles are identical. 2-Citizens may accept foreign titles with consent. 3-Excellence awards take no prefix. Correct set?
why: Awards encourage excellence while titles confer rank: different legal species. Citizens face an outright bar, and the no-prefix rule completes the scheme. Each claim fails on a different axis.
trapnote: Three statements, three distinct doctrines: test each independently.

q: A public authority denies a foreigner entry to a State-funded community hall on caste grounds, claiming a classification permitted by law with no recorded basis. Which combination resolves it?
options: Person-based equality controls; citizen-only access fails; unreasoned classification fails
expl: Three doctrines converge on one answer.
why: The challenger being foreign routes to person-based equality, knocking out the citizen-only access clause. The caste ground triggers the listed-access analysis for State-funded premises. The unrecorded basis fails both limbs of valid classification plus the arbitrariness test. All three must align.
trapnote: Synthesis questions punish single-doctrine answers; check person, ground and reasoning together.
